basis: Inherited renal tubular disorders of aldosterone response or electrolyte handling; salt, potassium and acid-base disturbances define the group.
Skeletal dysplasia, retinal dystrophy and antibody deficiency define syndrome; developmental delay 5/6. Dermatitis and hypogonadism (30-79%) omitted at cap.
Chronic adrenal cortical hormone deficiency; autoimmune disease is only one subtype. Pigmentation and electrolyte changes do not establish other organ damage.
Anophthalmia and esophageal atresia define the syndrome; cryptorchidism affects reproductive organs outside the axes.
Carcinoma confined to the breast, which has no axis.
Axonal sensory-autonomic neuropathy arising from an inherited sphingolipid biosynthesis disorder. Ulcers and osteomyelitis are secondary complications; cataract is not established as common.
Disease of the atrioventricular node, part of the cardiac conduction system.
Congenital hearing loss and skin/hair pigment abnormalities define the syndrome. Iris pigmentation does not establish visual damage; bowel and neurologic disease are minority subtype features.
Malignant B-cell precursors involve blood and marrow. This concept is leukemia; lymphoid lineage alone does not establish an immune mechanism axis.
Inherited ventricular electrical instability causes fibrillation despite the absence of structural heart disease.
Developmental delay, pulmonary cysts and Wilms tumors define GLOW; cysts and tumors reported in 2/2. Kyphosis and pectus deformity each occurred in 1/2.
Toxic injury causes obliteration of bronchioles; no infectious or autoimmune mechanism is specified.
Necrosis directly destroys the renal cortex; possible causes do not establish additional affected organs.
Progressive cerebellar and pyramidal dysfunction. Abnormal saccades and torticollis are neurologic manifestations rather than intrinsic eye or muscle damage.
Inherited cobalamin metabolic disorder; encephalopathy, profound developmental impairment and seizures in 1/1. Refractive error and esotropia alone provide uncertain evidence of direct ocular damage.
Cerebral arterial amyloid deposition with recurrent intracerebral hemorrhage defines the disease. Systemic deposits alone do not establish functional damage elsewhere.
Adenocarcinoma originates in gallbladder glandular epithelium; the gallbladder belongs to the hepatic axis.
Impaired intrahepatic bile flow directly affects the liver and biliary system.
Developmental impairment and brittle/fine hair define syndrome; fine hair in 3/4. Type II diabetes in 2/4 is a separate diagnosis without established direct endocrine injury; aneurysm 1/4.
Occlusion directly affects the carotid artery. Cerebral infarction is a possible separately diagnosed complication, not required by this concept.
EBV infection defines the mechanism. Across this broad concept, symptomatic mononucleosis and hepatitis cannot be assumed; hepatitis is also a separately defined disease.
Sebaceous carcinoma originates in the ocular adnexa, typically eyelid glands; eyelids are included in the ocular axis.
Progressive heterotopic ossification defines FOP; alopecia and hearing impairment each 30-79%. Respiratory insufficiency reflects chest-wall restriction rather than direct pulmonary injury.
Mutase deficiency causes organic acidemia; developmental impairment/dystonia and immunodeficiency each 30-79%. Renal insufficiency, optic atrophy and cardiomyopathy are 5-29%.
Mitochondrial metabolic dysfunction; neurodevelopmental regression in 5/5. Visual loss in 2/5 (40%), with optic atrophy documented; hearing impairment is very rare.
